items.headline: WPA Day 90 Arrives Without Escalation; Gottheimer Introduces 10th WPA Resolution (No Vote); Iran 'Broad Principles' 60-Day MOU Agreed at Negotiator Level — Khamenei Approval Gap Persists Day 3; Trump 'Time Is On Our Side'
items.summary: The War Powers Act hard 90-day constitutional deadline arrived today (Friday May 29) without the feared escalation scenario. No emergency congressional session was announced, no Senate 10th WPA resolution was voted on, no White House Counsel or DOJ OLC public statement on Day 90 legal posture was issued, and no CENTCOM repositioning or kinetic resumption signal materialized. House Democrats, led by Rep. Josh Gottheimer, introduced a new WPA resolution on Day 90 — the de facto 10th attempt since March — but no floor vote has been scheduled. The administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture (invoked May 1) holds as operative legal framing. The naval blockade (Day 48), CENTCOM self-defense authority, and physical Hormuz closure (Day 91) remain operative. Enforcement of the WPA's withdrawal requirement absent a court ruling or congressional action — neither of which materialized today — leaves the administration's posture effectively intact for the near term. Multiple Senate Democrats have signaled intent to litigate (novel constitutional theory; years to resolve). The bipartisan House majority (Rep. Golden plus six Republicans) remains real but unactivated, with House Republican leadership deferring the next war powers vote to early June — now past the hard deadline. On Iran: CBS News and Axios report that US-Iranian negotiators have agreed to the 'broad principles' of a 60-day MOU — a ceasefire extension plus kick-start of formal nuclear negotiations. Iran's own characterization of the draft deal (Al Arabiya) confirms that Hormuz shipping would gradually reopen in parallel with the US ending the naval blockade, with commercial shipping resuming within one month of signing. Trump stated 'time is on our side,' signaling a shift from the urgency-threat posture of May 24-28. The deal 'hangs on Trump and Khamenei approval' (JPost) — working-level alignment achieved but supreme-leader endorsement outstanding. The Shamkhani 'fantasy' nuclear-control statement (May 27) extends to Day 3 without Khamenei direct public contradiction or Araghchi formal text. Critically, the 60-day MOU framework defers the nuclear architecture question to a structured negotiation window rather than requiring a nuclear commitment at the MOU stage — this reduces the immediate Khamenei nuclear veto risk compared to a final-deal framework, and may explain why working-level agreement was reachable despite the Shamkhani statement.

May 28 market close: S&P 500 and Nasdaq set new records (7,563.63 and 26,917.47) despite the highest PCE reading in nearly three years — markets pricing deal optimism as the dominant signal. Warsh Day 15 silent; Kashkari (Minneapolis Fed, CNBC May 28) hawkish; June FOMC 18 days away without Chair guidance; personal saving rate at 2.6% — lowest since June 2022. PNW: Portland reversed from Thursday's confirmed 80°F to approximately 61°F today — temperature turbulence — before NWS tracking Sunday (May 31) rebound toward 90°F. Oregon fire season Day 22; T-3 to June 1 east Cascades NIFC above-normal onset. Bureau of Reclamation rationing Day 9. Israel-Lebanon ceasefire Day 13 holding. CISA clean streak Day 26. Reconciliation 2.0 June 1 Senate floor target T-3. Measles national estimated ~2,020 with school exposure window active 9 more days. Compound PNW stress vector — Friday's 61°F cooling is a temporary interlude; Sunday 90°F rebound + fire Day 22 + June 1 onset T-3 + Bureau of Reclamation Day 9 + PCE escalation + gas records + labor uncertainty + Portland budget T-33 + measles school window — maintains highest coherence of the conflict cycle. Vibe 3 holds. Khamenei formal MOU endorsement is the dominant forward signal.
